aria: Animated recap of the Pistons' 105 to 93 road win over the Spurs: Daniss Jenkins' 3-pointer off an Ausar Thompson steal with 1:45 left that made it 100 to 90, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Cade Cunningham's 27 points, the top scorers, how the Pistons won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from the Pistons' 105–93 road win over the San Antonio Spurs on Nov 17, 2026, from the Covers box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via WRAL), the Detroit Free Press, MLive and the San Antonio Express-News (all via Yahoo Sports), VAVEL and Ball Exclusives (via Yardbarker). All 105 Detroit points and all 93 San Antonio points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (26–29–23–27 to 33–21–18–21) add up to both totals: 55–54 Detroit at the half (AP; MLive). Team totals (points in the paint 60–44, fast-break points 24–15, assists 31–25, steals 10–4, threes 6 of 25 to 9 of 40) are from the box score; the paint edge of 16 matches ClutchPoints. San Antonio's biggest lead, 14, is from the box score and the AP, Free Press and Express-News; Detroit's, 12, is from the box score. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Tuesday's games.

Detroit ended San Antonio's 12-game winning streak; the Spurs had not lost since Oct. 23 (AP; Express-News). Detroit erased the 14-point deficit with a 21-7 run in the second quarter and closed the half on a 13-5 burst while Victor Wembanyama sat (AP). Cade Cunningham's steal and fast-break dunk came with 11.4 seconds left in the half (Free Press). Daniss Jenkins scored 21 of his 25 in the second half (AP). Wembanyama had 10 of his 25 in the first quarter (AP). Detroit played without Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson and Isaiah Joe (AP; Free Press). Detroit plays at New Orleans on Wednesday, Nov 18 at 8:00 PM ET (Ball Exclusives).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Daniss Jenkins' 3-pointer with 1:45 left that made it 100–90 (Free Press). Ausar Thompson grabbed a steal and passed to Jenkins for the three that put Detroit up 10 (MLive; VAVEL lists the three off a Thompson pass). Dylan Harper's drive had cut it to 95–90 with 2:36 left and Cunningham answered with a fadeaway jumper before Jenkins' threes (Express-News), so the board shows Pistons +7 to +10. It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc; the spot and the defender are not drawn to exact positions. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Detroit Pistons or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Daniss Jenkins' listed 6-foot-4 and 165 pounds with No. 24 (RealGM); no wingspan from a named measurement was found, so his arms use the default length. He is drawn in Detroit's road colors with the default figure look (no approved look yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
